title.value: Adaptive Discrete Communication Bottlenecks with Dynamic Vector Quantization
title.justification: The paper's title, as found in the provided text, is 'Adaptive Discrete Communication Bottlenecks with Dynamic Vector Quantization'.
title.quote: Adaptive Discrete Communication Bottlenecks with Dynamic Vector Quantization

extractions.description: The paper proposes a method called Dynamic Vector Quantization (DVQ) that dynamically selects the tightness of communication bottlenecks in neural networks. This approach aims to adaptively regulate the number of discrete codes and codebook size based on input complexity, enhancing model generalization and performance in tasks like visual reasoning and multi-agent reinforcement learning. By integrating key-query attention and Gumbel-softmax, the method improves communication efficiency among model components and agents, compared to fixed bottleneck vector quantization methods.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on deep learning, vector quantization, and communication bottlenecks within neural networks to improve model generalization and performance. While these areas can indirectly contribute to applications relevant to sustainable development, such as optimizing systems for energy efficiency or autonomous agents, the paper does not explicitly address climate or ecological sustainable development as a central theme.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Vector Quantization (VQ) is a method for discretizing latent representations and has become a major part of the deep learning toolkit... We show that dynamically varying tightness in communication bottlenecks can improve model performance on visual reasoning and reinforcement learning tasks.

primary_category.quote: In summary, the contributions of our work are as follows: • We propose a dynamic vector quantization method (DVQ) that adaptively chooses the number of discrete codes and the codebook size that control tightness of the bottleneck. • Our theoretical analysis shows that dynamic adjustment of the bottleneck improves generalization error under the sufficient condition of tighter average bottleneck and equal training loss.

applications.justification: The paper explicitly mentions how the dynamic vector quantization method can improve model performance specifically in visual reasoning and reinforcement learning tasks.
applications.quote: We empirically show improvement in performance by using DVQ to discretize inter-component communication within a deep learning model and inter-agent communication between agents, compared to using VQ with fixed bottleneck capacity.
